product_family: AI professional headshot generator (consumer, teams/corporate, and API)

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type 2 (corroborated in Master Service Agreement)
certifications.proof_quote: HeadshotPro maintains administrative, technical, and organizational measures...and operates a SOC 2 Type II program for relevant processes.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No ISO 27001 claim appears on the trust center, security policy, or any vendor page.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No HIPAA claim on any vendor page; consumer headshot tool, not a covered-entity / PHI use case.

certifications.name: GDPR (regulatory compliance posture, not a certification)
certifications.proof_quote: This policy is fully compliant with the European General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), as well as related laws and regulations in place at Singapore.

privacy.ai_training_note: Default is NO training. MSA states: 'Neither Customer Content nor AI Headshots will be used to train or retrain HeadshotPro's or any third party's generative models without Customer's explicit opt-in consent.' Processing is limited to 'provide, maintain, secure, and support the Service.' Customer is assigned ownership of generated AI Headshots and retains full commercial rights.
privacy.data_region: United States (Google Cloud Storage us-east-1; Render hosted on AWS). Note: privacy policy references GDPR and Singapore law, a minor inconsistency vs the US hosting stated in the Security Policy.

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: Yes — 'Q1 2025 HeadshotPro Pentest' document available on trust center (request access); controls list confirms 'Penetration testing findings remediated'.

security.name: Bug bounty program
security.value: None found (no HackerOne or Bugcrowd). Security Policy requires explicit advance written authorization before any pentest/assessment by third parties.

security.name: Authentication / MFA
security.value: Mandatory 2FA and strong password policy across GitHub, Render, GCS, Vercel; MFA required for critical services.

security.name: Web Application Firewall + VPN
security.value: WAF used; VPN used (per trust center controls)

security.name: Monitoring
security.value: Sentry application monitoring; access logging to apps and production consoles; audit logs collected.

security.name: Data retention / deletion
security.value: Input photos deleted after 7 days; AI headshots deleted after 30 days; user can self-delete anytime from account settings.

security.name: Payment processing
security.value: Handled by Stripe (no card data stored by vendor).

security.name: Subprocessors / infrastructure
security.value: Google Cloud Storage, Render (AWS), Vercel; sub-processor list published.

products.name: HeadshotPro Individual
products.data_scope: User uploads 1-3+ selfies; photos deleted after 7 days, headshots after 30 days; full commercial rights assigned to user; no model training without opt-in.

products.name: HeadshotPro for Teams / Corporate
products.data_scope: Same data handling and deletion policy; multi-tenant with logical separation; DPA + Master Service Agreement available for business buyers.
products.notes: Used by SMBs through Fortune 500; case studies cite multi-office rollouts. SOC 2 Type 2 + DPA support procurement review.

products.name: HeadshotPro API
products.data_scope: Programmatic headshot generation embedded into partner products; same no-training-by-default and deletion commitments via MSA.
products.notes: Used by partners to build scalable headshot solutions (e.g., real-estate case study).

compare.pricing_model: One-time per-package consumer pricing (no subscription); team discounts up to 60%; separate API access
compare.data_residency: United States (GCS us-east-1 + Render/AWS); no published EU data-residency option despite GDPR posture

flags: Minor inconsistency: Privacy Policy cites GDPR + Singapore law while Security Policy states US-only hosting (GCS us-east-1, Render/AWS). No EU data-residency option published.

SOC 2 Type 2 report and Q1 2025 pentest are gated behind 'Request access' on the Oneleet-powered trust center; status is publicly displayed as Compliant but the report itself was not directly inspected.
No public bug-bounty program; third-party security testing requires prior written authorization.
